Oil prices jump after OPEC+ announces surprise output cut

Published 2026-10-07 03:15 UTC

Oil prices jumped on Monday after OPEC+ unexpectedly announced it would cut production by 1 million barrels a day starting next month. Brent crude rose 6% to above $90 a barrel for the first time since spring, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate gained 5.8% to $86.

The group of oil-producing nations, led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, said the cut was a precautionary measure aimed at supporting market stability. Analysts had expected the group to keep output steady at its meeting, and the surprise caught traders who had been betting on lower prices because of slowing demand in China and rising U.S. production.

Energy stocks rallied on the news. Shares of major integrated oil companies rose between 3% and 5%, and oil service firms gained even more. Airline stocks fell because higher fuel costs eat into their profits, and shares of cruise operators and trucking companies also declined.

Economists warned that the cut could push up gasoline prices within weeks. Higher fuel costs would add to consumer inflation at a time when central banks are trying to bring price growth back to their targets. One estimate suggested U.S. pump prices could rise by 15 to 20 cents a gallon by the end of the month if crude stays near current levels.

Some analysts questioned whether all members will comply with the new quotas. Several countries have produced above their targets in past agreements, and the group's ability to enforce cuts has been limited. Others noted that U.S. shale producers could respond to higher prices by drilling more, which would offset part of the reduction over time.

The International Energy Agency said in a statement that the decision adds uncertainty to the market during the winter heating season. It urged producers to consider the impact on importing countries. The White House said it was monitoring the situation and that all options remain available to limit price increases for consumers.
